newsitem.title: UK: Dry cargo freight rates extend their slide.
newsitem.headline: Dry cargo freight rates extend their slide.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) posted a loss of five more points on Tuesday to a fresh four-year low of 1,051.

Brokers continue to say available tonnage mainly in the Panamax sector is weighing on the dry cargo freight market through to November when grain shipments may pick up. Some suggested that U.S. Gulf/Japan could ease to $18 short-term for want of grain orders. But fixtures reported on Tuesday for that route for October loading suggested owners might expect the market to steady compared with Monday's reported Korea Line fixing of Polska Walczaca for 54,000 tonnes at $19.20 no combination for September 15-25.

Halla is said to have fixed 54,000 tonnes heavy grain U.S. Gulf/Japan for 15-30 October at $20.40 without combination. Reports also said that Dorval last week fixed 52,000 tonnes U.S. Gulf/Japan for October 1-15 at $20.00 without combination.

"I do not know how far this points to anything significant," said one source. "The important thing from the owners' point of view is that activity has picked up a little. "But I would not want to bet on whether that will translate into better fixtures. It may encourage resistance by the owners which would be the important thing from their point of view". Japanese grain importers meanwhile have been sidelined on expectations of lower rates and the market will watch to see if the next few days show charterers emerging on a view that the bottom has been reached. "We don't expect a further sharp drop, say, to the $17 level...our impression is that the freight rates are to hover between $19 and $23 throughout this year" an analyst at Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd in Tokyo said on Tuesday.
Biffex futures also eased with most active October down 10 at 1,190 by 1500 gmt in thin volume of 89 lots.
